measures.transcript: Why the groove was neededA gear shaper strokes a disc cutter along each tooth. To finish the tooth, the cutter has to travel past the end of the face and throw its chip into open space, so the original shaft had a narrow groove just below the gear. That groove is the undercut in this story: the cutter runout and relief groove, distinct from the involute tooth-root undercut of a gear tooth.Material attemptsThree materials were tried in the grooved blank: AISI 4140 (40-45 HRC), AISI 4340 (48-50 HRC), and C300 (56-58 HRC). Each attempt was marked FAILED; these attempts are recounted by the designer.Changing the processThe failed groove design was replaced by a revised smooth blank, cut by rotary hobbing so all ten teeth formed with the approved lead-out. The revised shaft is AISI 4340 (H.T. 48-50 HRC), shown with an illustrative stress concentration rather than a certified result.Moving the supportsWith the new geometry settled, the bearing and retaining-ring pair moved 2.75 millimetres into the approved final placement beside a matching housing support, and the revised assembly study returns around the operating gear train.Material sequenceAISI 4140 (40-45 HRC): FAILEDAISI 4340 (48-50 HRC): FAILEDC300 (56-58 HRC): FAILEDAISI 4340 (H.T. 48-50 HRC), revised geometry

measures.transcript: Why the groove was neededA gear shaper strokes a disc cutter along each tooth. To finish the tooth, the cutter has to travel past the end of the face and throw its chip into open space, so the original shaft had a narrow groove just below the gear. That groove is the undercut in this story: the cutter runout and relief groove, distinct from the involute tooth-root undercut of a gear tooth.Material attemptsThree materials were tried in the grooved blank: AISI 4140 (40-45 HRC), AISI 4340 (48-50 HRC), and C300 (56-58 HRC). Each attempt was marked FAILED; these attempts are recounted by the designer.Changing the processThe failed groove design was replaced by a revised smooth blank, cut by rotary hobbing so all ten teeth formed with the approved lead-out. The revised shaft is AISI 4340 (H.T. 48-50 HRC), shown with an illustrative stress concentration rather than a certified result.Moving the supportsWith the new geometry settled, the bearing and retaining-ring pair moved 2.75 millimetres into the approved final placement beside a matching housing support, and the revised assembly study returns around the operating gear train.Material sequenceAISI 4140 (40-45 HRC): FAILEDAISI 4340 (48-50 HRC): FAILEDC300 (56-58 HRC): FAILEDAISI 4340 (H.T. 48-50 HRC), revised geometry
